# Native Muscle-Model Artifact Admission

## Status and Purpose

Evidence class: observed structural facts, provisional. Child #11819 of F07
#11791 adds `tour_matching.audit_muscle_model_asset` before expensive native
optimization. This inventory is not anatomical, physiological, contact or replay
qualification. The calculation registry and manual release remain blocked.

The boundary reuses `validate_model_checkpoint`, native OpenSim `Model` loading
and recursive component inheritance queries. It does not convert a model, change
parameters, equilibrate muscles or integrate dynamics. Successful `initSystem`
establishes initialization on this runtime, not an admissible replay checkpoint.

## Source and Loaded Identity

The caller supplies the complete SHA-256 of source `.osim` bytes. The source is
checked before parsing, against the captured bytes and after native inventory.
Mismatch raises an error. This detects ordinary concurrent modification, not an
adversarial change-and-restore race or a filesystem transaction.

The reader accepts native C++ scoped tags such as
`HuntCrossleyForce::ContactParametersSet` without XML namespace interpretation.
DTDs, entities and external XML references remain forbidden. Source bytes are
never rewritten. Class-name suffixes identify only XML declarations; omitted
properties remain null and plugin inheritance remains unresolved.

Native initialization records the actual OpenSim version, SHA-256 of
`model.dump()`, state names, coordinate facts and effective muscle options. A
second SHA-256 binds those observations with the version using deterministic
JSON. Caller region labels do not change this loaded identity. It covers recorded
serialization and observations, not compiled binaries, plugin provenance or
complete external resources. Those remain required before replay acceptance.

## Structural Observations

Recursive traversal reports exact native paths/classes for muscles, all forces,
nonmuscle actuators, controllers, constraints, contact geometry, bodies and other
components. Forces outside ForceSet remain visible. Actuator names do not prove
reserve, physiological-support or passive roles; their disposition is unverified.
Muscles outside the native muscle registry are reported separately and require
registration resolution; recursive presence alone does not prove control access.

Each muscle records its concrete law and effective `ignore_tendon_compliance`
and `ignore_activation_dynamics`. Geometric paths provide point-parent and
base-frame paths; non-geometric paths are explicitly unavailable. Conditional
point activation, wrapping, continuity, moment arms and force capacity are not
tested. For caller-declared regional frames $R_r$ and muscle attachment frames
$P_m$, the reported set is only

$$
A_r = \{m : P_m \cap R_r \ne \varnothing\}.
$$

Membership does not establish joint crossing, moment-arm sign or muscle action.
Unknown native frame paths fail, and unresolved muscle paths remain listed.
Region labels and coordinate roles are caller declarations, never inferred from
names or counts. Every region remains `anatomy_status = unverified`.

Coordinate facts include native initialized locks/prescription, default values
in their native units and exact declared roles. Native `nq` and `nu` are recorded
separately; they are not independent DOF counts because constraint rank is
unverified. No coordinate is universally relabelled as radians or degrees.

## Resources and Unavailable Evidence

Visual `Mesh.mesh_file` and `ContactMesh.filename` candidates are checked beside
the source and in its `Geometry` directory. Existing files are hashed and labelled
`local-candidate-unverified-use`; missing candidates stay missing. This does not
validate their contents or prove native selection over global search paths.
Other file/plugin dependencies and complete resource closure remain required.

Missing bindings yield `native-unavailable`; native load/connection/initialization
failure yields `native-load-failed`. Both retain source facts, declared maps and a
native-initialization requirement. Source-only requests yield `serialized-only`;
success yields `native-initialized-structural-only`. Every result remains
scientifically `unqualified`, requiring license/ancestry, resources,
anatomy/capacity, paths/parameters, full-state replay, contact and grip evidence.

## Verification and Reproduction

```python
from src.engines.physics_engines.opensim.python.tour_matching import (
    audit_muscle_model_asset,
)

inventory = audit_muscle_model_asset(
    local_osim_path,
    independently_pinned_sha256,
    region_frames=reviewed_region_frame_declarations,
    coordinate_roles=reviewed_coordinate_role_declarations,
)
facts = inventory.as_dict()
```

Run `python3 -m pytest tests/opensim/test_model_admission.py -o addopts='' -q`
with the pinned native environment. Synthetic native cases cover Millard/Thelen
options, locks, coupled constraints, auxiliary actuators, controllers, contact
geometry, forces outside ForceSet, repeated/changed identities, mapping errors
and load failure. Native cases skip when bindings are absent; such a run proves
only pure contracts. The turnover records actual native execution separately.

A generated 520-declaration source counterexample retains omitted properties,
locked wrist-like structure, extra actuators and missing geometry without claiming
full-body anatomy. No foreign model or private capture bytes are committed.
These checks complete neither F07/F08, D03 nor the all-model six-engine goal.
